explanations: Ball bearings, pneumatic tyres, chain-driven sprockets and tension-spoked wheels were first invented for it, then used in the car.
The upright safety shape has changed little since the first chain-driven model of around 1885.
It was invented in Europe in the 19th century, and by the early 21st century there were more than a billion of them.
In many regions it is the principal means of transport, as well as a machine for sport and recreation.
It is a human-powered, pedal-driven, single-track vehicle with two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other.

sources.excerpt: Several components that played a key role in the development of the car were initially invented for use in the bicycle, including ball bearings, pneumatic tires, chain-driven sprockets, and tension-spoked wheels.
The basic shape and configuration of a typical upright or "safety" bicycle, has changed little since the first chain-driven model was developed around 1885.
The bicycle was invented in Europe in the 19th century. By the early 21st century, there were more than 1 billion bicycles.
Bicycles are the principal means of transport in many regions.
A bicycle, also called a pedal cycle, bike, push-bike or cycle, is a human-powered or motor-assisted, pedal-driven, single-track vehicle, with two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: a motorcycle is single-track with two wheels but is not human-powered and did not carry the first chain-driven safety design; a tricycle has three wheels; a penny-farthing is an early form, but the clues point at the safety shape that followed it.
